Sometimes it becomes really tough to distinguish between stale fishes and a fresh catch. It can grow harder especially for newbies and upcoming kitchen enthusiasts just like me. But recently I have found my saviour to this problem! And that's 'Cambay Tiger'. No, it is not associated with Onitsuka Tiger in any way :)
Cambay Tiger is a premium store that offers wide range of fresh fishes and different types of meat to choose from.
I got to know from the manager that their  parent company is into this business since 1997. That makes them almost a 30 years old entity in this space.
Initially they became famous for their fresh & enormous sized Tiger Prawns and thus 'Tiger' in their store name.
I have been buying all my meat and seafood essentials from this store only since past 3-4 months and I just adore the service and quality I get every time.
They have their own aquaculture farm so you can be rest assured about the quality of the meat, its freshness and back tracking any product if you wish to.
They follow a 'farm-to-fork' business model and so you can get all your cooking needs under one roof, be it meat, fishes, spices, ready to cook curries, masalas etc.
All the fishes and meat products are cleaned thoroughly before packing them in the most hygienic fashion.
All in all, it's THE BEST place to go if you are looking for a one-stop-shop for your fish and meat requirements.
100% approved and recommended!

featured_reviews.name: Cyrus Doodhmal
featured_reviews.review_text:
Tucked away near Churchgate, the Bhikha Behram Well is a quiet oasis amid Mumbai’s bustle.

Built in 1725 by the Parsi Philanthropist Mr. Bhikha Behram, this old freshwater well has stood the test of time, offering both water and solace to those who visit.

Surrounded by trees and a peaceful enclosure, it feels like a step back in time—a place where sunlight filters through the leaves, casting dappled shadows on the worn stone floor.

For the Parsi community, it remains a sacred spot for prayers and reflection, its calm presence untouched by the city’s constant rush.

Timings  roughly 6:00 am onwards; morning hours are the main time when the wholesale and freshest stock comes.Locals recommend going around 6:00–7:30 am if you want the best catch and prices, especially if buying in bulk. Market layout and what you getThe market is divided into multiple sections: unloading/wholesale area on the road, a covered retail area where they also clean and cut, and open sections where you buy and then pay extra at cutting counters. You typically get a wide variety of saltwater fish like pomfret, surmai, bangda, bombil, prawns, crabs and seasonal catch, with both retail and wholesale options. Tips for visiting Go early, carry change, and be ready to bargain hard; prices are better if you buy in larger quantities.It is a traditional wet market, so expect crowds, strong smell, and wet floors. simple washable footwear and carrying your own bags can be more comfortable.If you tell what exactly you want (pomfret, prawns, bulk/retail, specific budget),

featured_reviews.name: Soniii
featured_reviews.review_text:
Churchgate railway station is one of the most iconic and lively places in Mumbai. More than just a railway station, it feels like the heart of South Mumbai where you can experience the real energy, beauty, and fast lifestyle of the city all together ✨

The moment you step out of Churchgate station, you instantly feel the charm of Mumbai. The busy streets, college students, office crowd, yellow-black taxis, old heritage buildings, and the cool sea breeze create a completely different atmosphere that feels both chaotic and beautiful at the same time

One of the best things about Churchgate is its perfect location. From here, you can easily explore some of the most famous places in Mumbai like Marine Drive, where people sit for hours enjoying the sea view and sunset. Just nearby, you can also visit Gateway of India, one of Mumbai’s most iconic landmarks, especially beautiful during evening lights.

For shopping lovers, Fashion Street is a paradise where you can find trendy clothes, shoes, bags, and accessories at affordable prices. If you enjoy history and art, the famous Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Vastu Sangrahalaya museum is also nearby and gives a glimpse into Mumbai’s rich culture and heritage.

Churchgate is also surrounded by amazing cafés, restaurants, and old Irani cafés that give classic Mumbai vibes. Whether it’s having coffee after a long day, walking near Marine Drive at night, or simply sitting and observing the city life, every moment here feels memorable ❤️

The station itself is always full of life. During rush hours, you can truly see how fast Mumbai runs. Thousands of people moving with purpose, trains arriving every few minutes, and still everything somehow feels organized in its own Mumbai style.

Personally, I feel Churchgate shows the perfect balance of modern city life and old Mumbai charm. It’s not just a place to travel from — it’s a place to experience. The aesthetic streets, sea view, nightlife, historical buildings, and nonstop city energy make Churchgate one of the most beautiful and unforgettable parts of Mumbai ✨

Churchgate railway station is southern most railway station and one of the most important railway stations of Mumbai. It is the terminus of western line of Mumbai Suburban railway.
It is very crowded during the peak hours. Trains arrive and depart frequently from the station in an interval of 2-3 minutes.
Most of the tourist places in Southern Mumbai like Marine Drive, Taj Hotel, Gateway of India, etc. are within 15 minutes travelling distance from the station.
The Fort area was initially an actual fort enclosure, the fort named Fort St. George. It had three main gates. One of these gates led straight to Saint Thomas Cathedral Church, hence it was named Church Gate. The fortress was eventually demolished in order to create new spaces for the expansion of the city, in 1860s. This gate was demolished in 1860. Later the Churchgate railway station was built in 1870 in close proximity to the position of the demolished gate, and hence got its name.

▪️Spring Roll - A well prepared fried rolls stuffed with grated carrot and cabbage was good in terms of taste.
▪️Baby Corn Salt & Papper - Deep fried babycorns cooked with spring onions, celery, ginger, garlic and plenty of black peppercorns was moreish and flavoursome.

Mains

▪️Water chestnuts with Green Pepper in sweet bean chilly sauce was delicious gravy preparation that added more taste with fried rice.

Mocktails

▪️Strawberry Sorbet - A perfectly made Margarita with crushed ice in strawberry flavour was chilled, sweet and awesome in taste.

Visited Society Restaurant inside Ambassador Hotel after ages to try their new oriental cuisine & the moment you step in you’ll be blown away with the elegance & class this place possesses.

My Veg Order was as follows : -

featured_reviews.name: Pankaj Kaklotar
featured_reviews.review_text:
A place that will take you back to the vintage Mumbai (Bombay)

The Society one of the restaurants and part of  ambassador hotel, is very classy and has very soothing ambience. We went to this place for a Saturday Lunch and we spent almost 3 to 4 hours talking, enjoying food and drinks.! Definitely one of the best place which will make you indulge in your conversations with friends, family and you won't realize the time.!

Talking more about Ambience, the society is a fine dine restaurant which makes you super comfortable in terms of seating! Beautiful bar counter, some green plants in corners and overall calmness flows through the place.!

Staff and Service! Mr. Om just made our day by that warm welcome with a big smile on his face. Staff at this place was very polite and well trained. Service was satisfying.!

Food and Drinks! Place offers a wide range of continental and oriental cuisines.! We just tried their oriental menu and it was satisfying overall. We could try few dishes, everything was prepared with fresh and high quality ingredients.!

Som tam - a very popular raw papaya salad with some cherry tomatoes and lot of spices.! Yeah, this is medium spicy salad with lot of health benifits.! If you haven't tried this one yet, go for it.!

Clear wonton soup - soup was good overall only thing I found wrong according to me was excessive layers of wonton in the soup.! If that could be little lesser would make it perfect. Taste wise it was perfect.!

Cottage cheese & Mushroom in Ginger chilly sauce - fresh cottage cheese and juicy mushrooms tossed perfectly in hot and spicy ginger chilly sauce, served piping hot, this was absolutely delightful.
*** Highly Recommended ***

Dimsums (shu mai style) - open head dimsums make it easy to stuff with sauces of choice and were perfectly steamed with fresh veggies stuffing.! Taste wise it was upto the mark.!

Eggplant cakes in hot bean sauce - so many dishes are there which would change your perception about eggplant.! This is one of them.! Those deep fried cakes were perfectly crisp and hot bean sauce was just enhancing taste like anything.! Overall a delicious dish.!

Waterchestnut in a sweet bean sauce - who all are fans of waterchestnuts? Don't miss this super delicious mains with juicy waterchestnuts and sweet bean sauce. Goes very well with the fried rice.!

Veg. Fried Rice - to accompany waterchestnuts and eggplant cake we ordered a veg friend rice. It was perfect fried rice I would say! Vegetables and rice everything in appropriate proportion.!

Whatever the scenario may be! There is always space for some desserts.! The Society has few unique and delightful desserts.!

Fried pan cakes - pan cakes stuffed with dates and deep fried! Served along with chocolate decor.! Tastes amazing and that crispness makes it more enjoyable.! Loved the presentation.!

Overall, a very calm place with some delicious otiental and continental delicacies. A good place for casual and official meet ups.!

I recently attended a wedding at Kora Kendar, and while the overall ambience was pleasant, I was disappointed with the lack of proper washroom facilities. Having previously visited for a garba event a few years ago, I expected improvements in this area, but unfortunately, it was still a major inconvenience.

The venue relies on portable restrooms, commonly known as porta-potties, which are known for their discomfort and lack of cleanliness. This arrangement was highly inconvenient, especially during a wedding where guests require comfortable and hygienic washroom facilities. The absence of proper washroom amenities significantly affected the overall experience.

However, it's worth noting that Kora Kendar does excel in terms of ambiance. The atmosphere created for the event was enjoyable, and the management seemed to have put effort into creating a pleasant environment for the guests. The overall decor and arrangements were satisfactory, contributing to the positive aspects of the venue.

Despite the shortcomings in washroom facilities, Kora Kendar may still be a suitable choice for events like garba or weddings, provided that alternative arrangements are made for washroom facilities. It would greatly enhance the overall experience and ensure the comfort of guests.

featured_reviews.name: Aditi Prabhu
featured_reviews.review_text:
Ambiance: Simple, soothing, with both indoor and outdoor sitting. Located at Babhai Naka, Borivali.

Our experience: We went in for dinner on a weekday. The place was largely empty and quiet. Took them 20 mins to take our first order despite having only 4 tables being served including ours.

We ordered the following dishes:
• Bombil Fry: The coating was way too thicker and the bombil hardly present. Could barely taste the bombil.
• Prawn koliwada: Again the coating overpowered the flavor of prawns.
• Bangda Thali and Ravas thali: Both thalis were exactly the same with the same fish curry, a tiny serving of prawn preparation, another tiny serving of matki usal in one thali and another random gravy in the bangda thalis. We weren't asked about our preferences for wada, chapati or bhakri. So one thali came with wadas, the other with chapati and on placing the order the third, we were asked about our preference for chapati or bhakri then informed bhakri is probabaly over. So we okayed chapati but were served wadas.

We also ordered another plate of extra chapati which they didnt have and offered wadas but none reached our table even after 2 reminders.

Finally we finished our meals and then asked for the bill which had the extra cost of wadas which we ordered and never recieved and also for the wada in thali which we weren't informed were charged extra but were given as they didnt have chapatis or bhakris.

They did change the bill on being informed.

We also asked for regular water which we recieved almost at the end of the meal after being reminded for the fifth time.

Service: Slow, and confused even when there were just 2-3 tables with people only.

While we understand it was end if the day and hence the food there was over and also probably that is why there were many errors & delays in service. But the overall experience and food were not upto the mark or hype.
